rules.statement: Don't report bounded per-key history as a memory leak, or ask for it to be dropped when the key goes idle, if that history is the documented replay window that resuming consumers rely on.
rules.why: Dropping the retained log of an emptied keyspace would turn a documented replay into a resync, and the memory saved is bounded and small.
rules.check: Before reporting retained history, check the docs and changelog for a promised replay or resume window that the retained entries implement.

rules.statement: Don't ask a unit test of a component's own internal rule (such as a compaction threshold) to stop asserting the exact value that rule produces.
rules.why: The test is the unit test of that rule, so changing the rule or its constants should change the test.
rules.check: Before reporting a test for pinning an internal threshold, check whether the test targets the type that owns the rule rather than a caller of it.

rules.statement: Don't ask for separately named constants to be merged or derived from one another just because they share a value today, when each names a distinct limit.
rules.why: Deriving one limit from another lets a change to one silently resize the others.
rules.check: Before reporting duplicate numeric constants, check whether each is a named constant in its own type with its own meaning (e.g. history kept vs. how far a consumer may lag).

rules.statement: Don't ask for a private constructor that is reached only through a static factory to become a primary constructor.
rules.why: A primary constructor is public, which would bypass the factory that does required work before construction.
rules.check: Before reporting a missing primary constructor, check whether the existing constructor is private or non-public and used only by a static factory.

rules.statement: Don't report sequential or guessable tokens as a security issue when the contract documents them as identifiers rather than credentials and they never cross a trust boundary.
rules.why: A token documented as "identifies a holder and is not a credential" only needs to be unique within the provider, and an in-process provider runs in the caller's own process.
rules.check: Before reporting a guessable token, read the token type's docs for whether it is a credential, and check whether it ever leaves the process or trust boundary.

rules.statement: Don't report a call made on the value that the previous call just returned (such as `.AsTask()`, `.GetAsyncEnumerator(token)` or `.Value`) as breaking the no-nested-calls or no-collaborator-chain rule.
rules.why: The convention bans only calls nested in another call's arguments and chains through collaborators (`a.B().C().D()`). Acting on a returned value is neither.
rules.check: Before reporting a chained call, check whether it is really a call inside another call's arguments or a walk through collaborators, and not just an operation on the value just returned.

rules.statement: Don't ask for short, similar code in several types to be pulled into a shared helper when the copies differ in how the item is identified and what the action does, so the helper would only take delegates and remove no logic.
rules.why: Such a helper adds indirection without removing logic. Only bookkeeping that really is the same across the types is worth sharing.
rules.check: Before reporting duplication, compare the copies: if each is two or three lines and differs in its key type and its action, don't report it.

rules.statement: Extract bookkeeping that is copied identically across several types, where only the key type and a final action differ, into one shared generic helper, and have each type supply only its own action.
rules.why: Otherwise a fix to one copy has to be repeated in every other copy, and the copies drift apart.
rules.check: Look for the same dictionary-of-sets bind/unbind/take logic or loop written out in several services.

rules.statement: Give a literal that is repeated across files or within a test (a token prefix, a test address) one named constant, and use that constant everywhere.
rules.why: Bare copies can drift apart, which leads to inconsistent formats or tests that pass or fail for the wrong reason.
rules.check: Look for the same string or number literal with the same meaning written in more than one place.

rules.statement: When a boolean property's computation changes, update its doc comment so that it states exactly when the value is true and when it is false.
rules.why: A caller who reads the old doc misinterprets the value and can't tell the different false cases apart.
rules.check: Compare a changed property expression with its <summary>, and check that every outcome that now makes it false is described.

rules.statement: In a conformance or contract test suite, cover stale-handle cases in each primitive: releasing or renewing a grant that has ended, or whose slot was granted again to another holder, returns false and leaves the new holder in place.
rules.why: A provider that matches only on the resource and slot, or that renews an ended grant, would otherwise pass the kit while admitting extra holders.
rules.check: For each ownership primitive in a contract suite, look for tests that release or renew a stale grant and assert false, and that waits complete on expiry and cancellation, as the sibling suites do.

rules.statement: In a test project, a test that expects an ArgumentException (or a subtype) keeps the exception and asserts its ParamName.
rules.why: Otherwise an unrelated argument failure satisfies the test and hides a broken check.
rules.check: Look for Assert.Throws/ThrowsAnyAsync of an ArgumentException type whose result isn't used to assert ParamName.

rules.statement: In a test project, test a size or length limit with input exactly at the limit, which succeeds, as well as with input just past it.
rules.why: An off-by-one that rejects input at exactly the limit would otherwise pass.
rules.check: For each limit+1 rejection test, look for a matching test that uses exactly the limit and asserts success.

rules.statement: In a test project, every test asserts something; a test that only checks a call doesn't throw uses `Assert.Null(Record.Exception(...))`.
rules.why: A test with no assertion lets misbehavior go unnoticed.
rules.check: Look for test methods with no Assert call, such as a test that disposes twice and checks nothing.

rules.statement: In a test project, move a helper that is copied into several test files into one shared test helper class, and call it from there.
rules.why: The copies can drift apart.
rules.check: Look for the same private helper method declared in more than one test file.

rules.statement: Apply the rule that async methods take a trailing CancellationToken to test-kit and test helper methods as well: they take the token and forward it, instead of reading the test context's token themselves.
rules.why: Otherwise the helpers are shaped inconsistently, and callers can't pass their own token.
rules.check: Look for async helpers in test or conformance-kit code that have no CancellationToken parameter or that read TestContext's token internally.

rules.statement: Take a lock scope with a `using var` declaration rather than a `using (...) { }` block or a `lock` statement, unless code after the locked part must run outside the lock; when it must, add a comment saying why.
rules.why: This keeps lock scoping consistent, and an undocumented block looks like a departure from the convention.
rules.check: Look for `lock (...)` or `using (X.EnterScope()) { }` blocks, and check whether any code after them has to run unlocked and whether a comment explains that.

rules.statement: Make a method return void when no caller uses its return value.
rules.why: An unused return value suggests that callers branch on it when none do.
rules.check: For a method with a non-void return in a diff, check whether any caller reads the result.

rules.statement: Don't implement paged listing by scanning, copying and sorting the whole collection on every page; keep an ordered index, seek to the continuation and read at most limit + 1 entries.
rules.why: A full scan and sort per page makes paging through a large collection quadratic.
rules.check: Look for list or page methods that enumerate and sort the full set and then skip to the continuation token.

rules.statement: When you edit a paragraph in a doc comment or a Markdown document, reflow the whole paragraph evenly to 120 columns without changing its words.
rules.why: Inserted text otherwise leaves short or overlong lines, the wrap is uneven, and a wrap check may flag it.
rules.check: Look at edited paragraphs for a short line in the middle of the paragraph or a line over 120 columns.
